Definition: from G5164; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct:--path.
BiblicalUsage: Hebrews tells the lame to make straight paths for their feet, lest what is lame be turned out of the way. Make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way, but let it rather be healed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse turns the old highway promise into a personal one: the path is for feet, and the healing is for the lame who walk it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
